title: COMPASS: Predicting the Relationship of Multiple Patches for Vulnerabilities with LLMs
title_zh: COMPASS：利用大语言模型预测多个漏洞补丁之间的关系

paragraphs.en: Modern software heavily relies on code reuse, so upstream vulnerability fixes do not automatically propagate to downstream codebases. Downstream maintainers must manually adopt patches to eliminate known risks. In practice, a single vulnerability often corresponds to multiple patches, which greatly complicates downstream patch adoption because different patch relationships imply different adoption strategies. To address this challenge, we first manually inspect large-scale multi-patch vulnerabilities ( ∼ \sim 1K) in the real world and interview experienced developers , summarizing six typical types of patch relationships, i.e., Merge , Mirror , Better Solution , Fixing-of-Fixing , Collaboration , and Separation . Based on these observations, we propose COMPASS, an automated approach that predicts the relationships of multiple vulnerability patches with large language models. Given a CVE as input, COMPASS follows a four-phase pipeline that ( i ) identifies the patch group and pre-scans explicit relationships , ( ii ) performs individual patch analysis, ( iii ) infers relationship instances via a hierarchy-guided prompt, and ( iv ) validates completeness and consistency of the inferred results. As output, COMPASS reports the predicted relationships within the patch group and visualizes them as a relationship graph. We evaluate COMPASS on a benchmark of 300 multi-patch CVEs and compare it against mainstream learning-based and LLM baselines. Results show that our method achieves strong and consistent prediction effectiveness and outperforms SOTA by 85.04% on average. We publicly release an online querying website to support community reuse of patch relationships knowledge: https://patch-relation.com .

paragraphs.en: In the context of open-source environments, the general many-for-one fixing pattern in upstream software brings significant complexity to patch adoption for downstream projects that depend on it. The complexity is largely determined by the relationships of patches, as different relationships directly lead to different adoption strategies. Specifically, modern software development heavily relies on code reuse: many projects act as upstream software platforms whose code is copied, integrated, and customized by a large number of downstream projects, and upstream vulnerability fixes do not propagate to downstream code by default because the code between the upstream and downstream is disconnected [ 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 ] . Thus, when an upstream vulnerability is fixed, downstream projects need to manually adopt these patches. However, the decoupling caused by code copying, long-term independent evolution, and project-specific customization often makes upstream patches inapplicable or ambiguous, and more importantly, the many-for-one fixing pattern implies that these patches may play different roles and interact in complex ways. As a result, downstream maintainers must understand how these patches relate to each other (i.e., their relationships) before deciding how to adopt them [ 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 在开源环境中，上游软件中常见的“多对一”修复模式，使得依赖其的下游项目在采用补丁时面临显著复杂性。 这种复杂性主要由补丁之间的关系决定，因为不同的关系会直接导致不同的采用策略。 具体而言，现代软件开发高度依赖代码复用：许多项目充当上游软件平台，其代码被大量下游项目复制、集成和定制；而由于上下游之间的代码是断开的，上游的漏洞修复默认不会传播到下游代码中 [ 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 ] 。 因此，当上游漏洞得到修复时，下游项目需要手动采用这些补丁。 然而，由代码复制、长期独立演进以及项目特定定制所导致的解耦，常常使上游补丁无法适用或含义模糊；更重要的是，“多对一”的修复模式意味着这些补丁可能扮演不同角色并以复杂方式相互作用。 因此，下游维护者在决定如何采用这些补丁之前，必须理解它们彼此之间的关系（即其关系性）[ 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 ] 。

paragraphs.en: For example, if Patch- A A initially fixes a vulnerability but inadvertently introduces a new bug or vulnerability, and Patch- B B later fixes this issue, the two patches must be applied sequentially and released together, otherwise, releasing the two patches in different releases (e.g., due to the tight schedule, the capability of the maintenance team, or the limitation of available manpower) may expose users to new security risks. In another case, multiple patches may collaboratively fix a vulnerability step by step, where later patches just depend on variables or logic introduced by earlier ones. Such patches must be applied in order, but they can be released separately when necessary, because intermediate patches represent incomplete yet safe fixes that do not introduce new flaws. For another example, if Patch- A A provides a complete fix and Patch- B B merely optimizes the original solution (e.g., improving performance or code readability), downstream maintainers may choose to apply only the latter to avoid redundant work. In addition to the above example situations, there are more other cases where the relationship of patches largely participates in the vulnerability fixing, which will be given in Section II . These examples illustrate that different patch relationships imply fundamentally different adoption behaviors, and misunderstanding these relationships can lead to delayed or inconsistent decisions, and a higher risk of incomplete or even unsafe patch adoption.

Second, we feed the patch group (including the commit ID, the branch/version information, the commit message, and the code change of each patch) to LLMs, and guide LLMs to think about three questions using the intuition of chain-of-thought: ( i ) double-checking whether each patch directly fixes the vulnerability, ( ii ) identifying key components/files modified by the patches, and ( iii ) noting implicit signals available in commit messages and branch/version information. Third, we design a sophisticated prompt describing the summarized six relationships in the text form, and ask LLMs to predict the relationships of the fed patches according to given schema based on the thoughts. Fourth, LLMs are required to validate the prediction result to make sure that all patches have been predicted, no contradictory relationships, and so on. Finally, the relationships within the patch group will be output and further reorganized into a visualized graph to facilitate users’ understanding.

paragraphs.en: To evaluate the effectiveness of COMPASS, we construct a benchmark consisting of 300 vulnerability entries with 2 ∼ \sim 7 patches, which is completely disjoint from the 1,050 multi-patch vulnerability entries used for taxonomy construction. We further develop an online website to publicly host vulnerability entries together with the relationships of their multiple patches. This design is motivated by the observation that a single CVE can affect many downstream projects, and thus the relationships of its patches are often repeatedly queried by different teams, making a shared resource valuable for avoiding duplicated manual effort. The 300 benchmark entries have been uploaded as an initial release, and we will continuously maintain the website in the future. paragraphs.en: To describe how multiple patches associated with the same vulnerability relate to each other in the real world, we preliminarily inspected 1,050 multi-patch vulnerability entries from CVE [ 6 ] , NVD [ 7 ] , and Snyk [ 23 ] . We constructed the taxonomy of patch relationships by combining authors’ qualitative analysis with developer interviews. Specifically, we first derived an initial set of relationship patterns by examining vulnerability descriptions, commit messages, code changes, etc. We then invited 20 developers in top-tier Internet companies with at least seven years of experience in open-source development, security maintenance, or vulnerability fixing, to validate and refine the taxonomy. Specifically, we provided them with randomly-sampled multi-patch CVE cases and the candidate taxonomy, and asked whether the relationship types were understandable, practically meaningful for downstream patch adoption, and whether any recurring types were missing. Their feedback was used to refine the category boundaries and descriptions. This process resulted in six recurring and actionable relationship types: Merge , Mirror , Better Solution , Fixing-of-Fixing , Collaboration , and Separation . This taxonomy is intended to cover dominant practical patterns. Rare or highly context-specific relationships may exist beyond these types, but they do not affect the main findings of this work.
paragraphs.zh: 为了描述与同一漏洞相关的多个补丁在现实世界中如何相互关联，我们初步检查了来自 CVE [6]、NVD [7] 和 Snyk [23] 的 1,050 条多补丁漏洞条目。 我们通过结合作者的定性分析与开发者的访谈，构建了补丁关系分类体系。 具体来说，我们首先通过研究漏洞描述、提交信息、代码变更等内容，推导出一组初始的关系模式。 随后，我们邀请了 20 名来自顶级互联网公司的开发者参与验证和细化该分类体系，这些开发者在开源开发、安全维护或漏洞修复方面至少拥有七年经验。 具体来说，我们向他们提供了随机抽取的多补丁 CVE 案例和候选分类体系，并询问他们是否理解这些关系类型、这些类型对后续补丁采用是否具有实际意义，以及是否存在任何缺失的重复类型。 他们的反馈被用于完善各类别的边界和描述。 这一过程最终确定了六种具有重复性且可操作的关系类型：合并（Merge）、镜像（Mirror）、更优解决方案（Better Solution）、修复中的修复（Fixing-of-Fixing）、协作（Collaboration）和分离（Separation）。 该分类体系旨在涵盖主要的实践模式。 除了这些类型之外，可能还存在罕见或高度依赖具体情境的关系，但它们不会影响本研究的主要发现。

paragraphs.en: The above taxonomy construction follows common practice in empirical software engineering, where candidate concepts are first derived from empirical observations and then refined through human feedback. For example, Šmite et al. constructed a GSE (global software engineering) taxonomy by combining literature-based candidate terms with an expert survey, and showed that such empirically based taxonomies can support later research and decision-making [ 25 ] . Similarly, Doğan and Tüzün first manually collected code review bad practices from white and gray literature, then conducted interviews with experienced practitioners to refine the concepts, resulting in a taxonomy of code review smells that further supports tool development [ 26 ] . paragraphs.en: The Merge relationship describes a scenario in which vulnerability patches developed on different branches are subsequently integrated into a single branch through a branch merge. In this case, one patch consolidates the effects of multiple related patches that exist on separate development lines, resulting in a unified fix for the vulnerability. At the Git level, such a merge patch is sometimes identifiable by having more than one parent commit, and its code content is formed by integrating the changes introduced by patches on the merged branches into the target branch’s code history.
paragraphs.zh: 合并关系描述了一种场景：在不同分支上开发的漏洞补丁随后通过分支合并被整合到单个分支中。 在这种情况下，一个补丁会整合存在于不同开发线中的多个相关补丁的效果，从而形成对该漏洞的统一修复方案。 在 Git 层面，这类合并补丁有时可以通过其拥有不止一个父提交来识别，其代码内容则是通过将合并分支上的补丁所引入的变更整合到目标分支的代码历史中而形成的。

paragraphs.en: As defined in Git’s official documentation [ 30 ] and previous studies [ 21 , 31 , 17 , 12 , 32 ] , this mechanism is widely used to consolidate parallel vulnerability-fixing efforts. For downstream maintainers, recognizing this relationship helps identify the consolidated fix and avoid separately reasoning about each merged patch when the merge patch is applicable, reducing the manual effort required during patch adoption. We analyze a real-world example of this relationship (CVE-2014-1829 [ 33 ] , which reports a vulnerability in python-requests allowing remote servers to obtain a netrc password) in our supplementary document.
paragraphs.zh: 正如 Git 官方文档 [ 30 ] 和先前研究 [ 21 , 31 , 17 , 12 , 32 ] 所定义的那样，该机制被广泛用于整合并行进行的漏洞修复工作。 对于下游维护者而言，识别这种关系有助于确定已整合的修复方案，并在合并补丁适用时避免对每个合并的补丁单独进行推理，从而减少补丁采用过程中所需的人工工作量。 我们在补充材料中分析了一个现实世界中的此类关系示例（CVE-2014-1829 [ 33 ]，该漏洞存在于 python-requests 中，允许远程服务器获取 netrc 密码）。

paragraphs.en: The Mirror relationship describes a scenario in which identical or functionally equivalent vulnerability patches are independently applied to different versions (e.g., v 1.0 vs. v 2.0) or branches (e.g., main vs. feature ) of the same codebase. Although these patches address the same vulnerability, they belong to independent code evolution paths with unique commit histories and parent pointers.
paragraphs.zh: “镜像”关系描述了一种场景：相同或功能等效的漏洞补丁被独立地应用于同一代码库的不同版本（例如 v 1.0 与 v 2.0）或分支（例如 main 与 feature）。 尽管这些补丁解决了相同的漏洞，但它们属于独立的代码演化路径，具有独特的提交历史和父指针。

sents.en: The Mirror relationship describes a scenario in which identical or functionally equivalent vulnerability patches are independently applied to different versions (e.g., v 1.0 vs. v 2.0) or branches (e.g., main vs. feature ) of the same codebase.
sents.zh: “镜像”关系描述了一种场景：相同或功能等效的漏洞补丁被独立地应用于同一代码库的不同版本（例如 v 1.0 与 v 2.0）或分支（例如 main 与 feature）。

sents.en: Although these patches address the same vulnerability, they belong to independent code evolution paths with unique commit histories and parent pointers.
sents.zh: 尽管这些补丁解决了相同的漏洞，但它们属于独立的代码演化路径，具有独特的提交历史和父指针。

paragraphs.en: Mirror patches typically exhibit a high degree of similarity in their code changes. Minor differences may exist due to contextual factors, such as variations in surrounding code or line numbers across branches, but the underlying fixing logic remains equivalent. A typical mechanism that gives rise to this relationship is cherry-picking [ 34 , 17 ] , where a maintainer explicitly replicates a patch from one branch to another without merging the full branch history. For example, suppose a developer fixes a vulnerability with Patch P1 in a long-running feature branch. Since this branch is not yet ready for full merging but the fix is critical for the stable main branch, a maintainer uses “ git cherry-pick P1 ” to replicate the patch. This operation creates a new commit P2 in main that carries the exact code changes from P1 . In this case, P1 and P2 form a Mirror relationship. From the perspective of downstream maintainers, understanding this relationship helps them select the patch that matches the specific branch or version they depend on, without expending additional effort comparing multiple patches that are functionally equivalent. We analyze a real-world example of this relationship (CVE-2011-2931 [ 35 ] , which reports a cross-site scripting vulnerability in Ruby on Rails allowing attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts or HTML) in our supplementary document).

paragraphs.en: The Better Solution relationship describes a sequence of patches where a subsequent patch (can be denoted as P2 ) refines a prior patch (can be denoted as P1 ) by improving the implementation of the fix while preserving the same remediation mechanism for the vulnerability. Specifically, P2 focuses exclusively on improvements unrelated to the vulnerability fix itself, such as readability, maintainability, or performance (e.g., clarifying code comments, streamlining non-critical logic, or optimizing runtime efficiency), it does not alter the fundamental mechanisms that address the vulnerability (e.g., input validation rules, access control checks, or encryption implementations). P2 is typically dependent on P1 : it builds upon code structures, control logic, or functions introduced by P1 . While P2 may partially or even fully subsume P1 ’s implementation at the code level, it does not replace the original security responsibility, which remains anchored in P1 .
paragraphs.zh: “更优解决方案”关系描述了一系列补丁，其中后续补丁（可表示为 P2）通过改进修复方案的具体实现来优化先前的补丁（可表示为 P1），同时保留针对该漏洞的相同修复机制。 具体而言，P2 仅专注于与漏洞修复本身无关的改进，例如可读性、可维护性或性能（如澄清代码注释、简化非关键逻辑或优化运行时效率），它不会改变解决该漏洞的基本机制（如输入验证规则、访问控制检查或加密实现）。 P2 通常依赖于 P1：它建立在 P1 引入的代码结构、控制逻辑或函数之上。 尽管 P2 在代码层面可能部分甚至完全取代 P1 的实现，但它并未替代最初的安全责任，该责任仍由 P1 承担。

From the perspective of downstream maintainers, the initial patch is usually sufficient to eliminate the vulnerability and can be applied promptly in time-sensitive scenarios, while later patches may be considered optionally to improve code quality or performance based on maintenance needs. We analyze a real-world example of this relationship (CVE-2014-1830 [ 36 ] , which reports a vulnerability allowing remote servers to obtain sensitive user credentials) in our supplementary document.
paragraphs.zh: 这种关系通常出现在后修复优化阶段，即最初的补丁在发布后经过进一步打磨，以支持长期维护或提升效率。 从下游维护人员的角度来看，初始补丁通常足以消除漏洞，并能在时间敏感的场景中迅速应用；而后续补丁则可根据维护需求，视情况选择采用，以进一步提升代码质量或性能。 我们在补充文档中分析了一个此类关系的实际案例（CVE-2014-1830 [ 36 ]，该漏洞允许远程服务器获取敏感的用户凭证）。

paragraphs.en: The Fixing-of-Fixing relationship describes a scenario in which a subsequent patch corrects flaws that are unintentionally introduced by an earlier patch. In this relationship, the initial patch aims to remediate the original vulnerability but introduces new vulnerabilities or functional bugs due to incomplete logic, overlooked edge cases, implementation errors, and so on. The later patch directly targets the newly introduced problem and relies on the code structures or logic established by the earlier patch to perform the correction.
paragraphs.zh: “修复的修复”关系描述了一种情形：后续的一个补丁修正了先前补丁无意中引入的缺陷。 在这种关系中，初始补丁旨在修复原始漏洞，但由于逻辑不完整、忽略边缘情况、实现错误等原因，反而引入了新的漏洞或功能错误。 后续补丁直接针对新引入的问题，并依赖先前补丁建立的代码结构或逻辑来完成修正。

sents.en: The Fixing-of-Fixing relationship describes a scenario in which a subsequent patch corrects flaws that are unintentionally introduced by an earlier patch.
sents.zh: “修复的修复”关系描述了一种情形：后续的一个补丁修正了先前补丁无意中引入的缺陷。

sents.en: In this relationship, the initial patch aims to remediate the original vulnerability but introduces new vulnerabilities or functional bugs due to incomplete logic, overlooked edge cases, implementation errors, and so on.

sents.en: The later patch directly targets the newly introduced problem and relies on the code structures or logic established by the earlier patch to perform the correction.
sents.zh: 后续补丁直接针对新引入的问题，并依赖先前补丁建立的代码结构或逻辑来完成修正。

paragraphs.en: Fixing-of-Fixing patches are inherently interdependent: applying only the initial patch may leave newly introduced vulnerabilities or bugs, while applying only the subsequent patch is ineffective without the foundational code it corrects. paragraphs.en: The Collaboration relationship describes a scenario in which multiple patches jointly resolve a vulnerability, while none of them is sufficient on its own. In this relationship, an earlier patch introduces foundational security mechanisms (such as core data structures, variables, or preliminary checks) that are necessary but incomplete for eliminating the vulnerability. One or more subsequent patches then build on this foundation, extending or completing the remediation logic so that their combined effect fully addresses the vulnerability. This relationship commonly arises when fixing complex vulnerabilities that require multi-stage remediation, for example those involving layered systems, interdependent components, or intricate control flows. For downstream maintainers, recognizing the collaboration relationship is important because it indicates that the patches are complementary and must be applied together to achieve a complete fix. We analyze a real-world example of this relationship (CVE-2020-25781 [ 38 ] , which reports a permission bypass vulnerability allowing users without access to private issue notes to download attached files via direct URLs) in our supplementary document.

paragraphs.en: The Separation relationship describes patches that address distinct aspects of a vulnerability or target the replicated vulnerable pattern across different locations within a codebase, without functional or code-level interdependence. In this relationship, patches operate on disjoint code regions, and no patch relies on code additions or modifications introduced by another. As a result, the corresponding patches serve distinct purposes, evolve independently, and can be applied in any order or in parallel without affecting correctness or security. paragraphs.en: The mission of COMPASS is to predict the relationships of multiple patches associated with a given vulnerability. COMPASS follows a four-phase pipeline for this goal. In Phase-1 ( Patch Group Extraction & Pre-Scanning ), the method takes a vulnerability entry from public platforms (e.g., CVE, NVD, Snyk) as input. These platforms typically record links to the patches that fix the vulnerability , allowing the required patch group to be obtained directly. After that, COMPASS determines some explicit patch relationships at an early stage via a pre-scanning step . Then, the vulnerability (including the CVE ID and the description) and its patch group (including the commit ID, the branch/version information, the commit message, and the code change of each patch) will be fed into an LLM under the intuition of chain-of-thought. In Phase-2 (Individual Patch Analysis), we ask the LLM to double-check the patch group provided by the vulnerability platform for further determining whether each patch directly fixes the vulnerability. And we also ask the LLM to identify key components and files modified, and note any implicit signals in patch information, to facilitate the following analysis. In Phase-3 (Patch Relationship Prediction), we send the description of the six types of patch relationships to the LLM, organize them into three hierarchies, and prompt the LLM to reason about relationships. In Phase-4 (Validation Check), the LLM is asked to revisit its previous predictions, ensuring that all patches have been predicted and verifying that there are no contradictory relationships. Finally, COMPASS integrates the reasoning results of the above thinking processes and organize the output according to the predefined schema. The overview of COMPASS is given in Figure 1 .
paragraphs.zh: COMPASS 的任务是预测与给定漏洞相关的多个补丁之间的关系。 为实现这一目标，COMPASS 遵循一个包含四个阶段的流程。 在第一阶段（补丁组提取与预扫描）中，该方法以公共平台（例如 CVE、NVD、Snyk）上的漏洞条目作为输入。 这些平台通常会记录修复该漏洞的补丁链接，从而可以直接获取所需的补丁组。 之后，COMPASS 会通过预扫描步骤在早期阶段确定一些明确的补丁关系。 接着，将漏洞信息（包括 CVE ID 和描述）及其补丁组（包括每个补丁的提交 ID、分支/版本信息、提交消息和代码变更）在“思维链”机制下输入 LLM。 在第二阶段（单个补丁分析）中，我们会要求 LLM 再次检查漏洞平台提供的补丁组，以进一步确定每个补丁是否直接修复了该漏洞。 同时，我们也会要求 LLM 识别被修改的关键组件和文件，并记录补丁信息中的任何隐含信号，以便后续分析。 在第三阶段（补丁关系预测）中，我们会将六种类型的补丁关系描述发送给 LLM，将其组织为三个层级，并提示 LLM 对关系进行推理。 在第四阶段（验证检查）中，我们会要求 LLM 重新审视其先前的预测，确保所有补丁都已被预测，并验证不存在矛盾的关系。 最后，COMPASS 会整合上述思维过程的推理结果，并按照预定义的 schema 组织输出。 COMPASS 的概述见图 1。

paragraphs.en: Taking as input a vulnerability entry from public vulnerability platforms (e.g., CVE, NVD, Snyk), Phase-1 aims to identify its patch group (which serves as the input for subsequent analysis) and directly determine explicit patch relationships at an early stage.
paragraphs.zh: 以公共漏洞平台（例如 CVE、NVD、Snyk）中的漏洞条目作为输入，第一阶段旨在识别其补丁组（该补丁组将作为后续分析的输入），并在早期直接确定明确的补丁关系。

paragraphs.en: Vulnerability entries in public platforms typically provide explicit links to patches, allowing COMPASS to directly obtain the patch group. Received the patch group, COMPASS performs a lightweight pre-scanning step over commit messages to identify explicit and high-confidence relationship evidence. For example, commit messages may contain indicative terms such as “ merge ”, “ merged in ”, or “ pull request ”, which strongly suggest the Merge relationship, or terms such as “ refactor ”, “ optimize ”, and “ improve performance ”, which often signal the Better Solution relationship [ 40 , 41 , 42 ] . Such indicators serve as explicit textual evidence about the intent of a patch and, when present, allow the corresponding relationships to be determined with high confidence at an early stage. Importantly, this pre-scanning step is only applicable when such explicit cues are present, which occurs in rare cases in real-world open-source projects [ 43 , 44 ] . Prior studies on security commit messages have shown that such messages are often insufficiently informative. For example, Abreu et al. reported that 56.7% of security commit messages were poorly documented [ 45 ] , and a large-scale replication study further confirmed that security commit messages remain not informative enough for security-focused tasks [ 46 ] . That is, many vulnerability patches lack explicit relationship cues in their commit messages, motivating to reason over code changes together with message semantics. For these majority cases, COMPASS proceeds with the LLM-based analysis pipeline (Phase-2 to Phase-4) to infer patch relationships.

sents.zh: 以往对安全提交信息的研究表明，这类信息通常不够详尽。

sents.en: For example, Abreu et al. reported that 56.7% of security commit messages were poorly documented [ 45 ] , and a large-scale replication study further confirmed that security commit messages remain not informative enough for security-focused tasks [ 46 ] .
sents.zh: 例如，Abreu 等人报告称，56.7% 的安全提交信息文档编写质量较差 [45]；一项大规模复现研究进一步证实，安全提交信息对于以安全为重点的任务而言仍不够详尽 [46]。

sents.en: That is, many vulnerability patches lack explicit relationship cues in their commit messages, motivating to reason over code changes together with message semantics.
sents.zh: 也就是说，许多漏洞补丁的提交信息中缺乏明确的关系提示，因此有必要结合代码变更与消息语义进行推理。

sents.en: For these majority cases, COMPASS proceeds with the LLM-based analysis pipeline (Phase-2 to Phase-4) to infer patch relationships.
sents.zh: 对于这些多数情况，COMPASS 将采用基于大语言模型的分析流程（第 2 至第 4 阶段）来推断补丁之间的关系。

paragraphs.en: Note that the aforementioned “direct relationship determination” in pre-scanning is performed at the relationship instance level. A relationship instance denotes a piece of relationship within a patch group, involving one or more patches. The resolved instances are not forwarded to the subsequent phases of COMPASS. As a reminder, each individual patch in such resolved instances is retained in the patch group, as it may also be involved in other unresolved relationship instances.

paragraphs.en: Patch-Vulnerability Alignment. Checking whether each patch in the patch group directly contributes to the remediation of the target vulnerability. This helps determine dependency-oriented relationships such as Better Solution , Fixing-of-Fixing , and Collaboration , because they are often characterized by a sequential fixing chain, where later patches may refine, correct, or build on prior patches.

paragraphs.en: The goal of Phase-2 is not to directly predict or output patch relationships. It serves as a structured analysis scaffold, guiding the LLM to inspect each patch in isolation and extract key signals that are essential for the subsequent relationship reasoning. paragraphs.en: COMPASS organizes patch relationship prediction into three hierarchies to guide the LLM through a structured reasoning process. Hierarchy-1 focuses on relationships that can be inferred from clear structural composition or high code-level similarity, Hierarchy-2 performs dependency-based reasoning, and Hierarchy-3 handles cases where no dependency is identified within the involved patch set.

paragraphs.en: COMPASS first asks the LLM to identify Merge and Mirror relationships, as these two types often exhibit comparatively clear characteristics in code changes and branch/version contexts. For Merge , the LLM checks whether a patch consolidates changes from multiple related patches on separate development lines, and distinguishes the merge patch from the merged patches, allowing downstream maintainers to easily identify the consolidated fix. For Mirror , the LLM checks whether patches implement identical or highly similar fixes across different software versions or branches, with high similarity in both code changes and commit messages.
paragraphs.zh: COMPASS 首先会要求 LLM 识别合并（Merge）和镜像（Mirror）关系，因为这两种关系在代码变更以及分支/版本上下文中通常表现出相对清晰的特点。 对于合并关系，LLM 会检查某个补丁是否整合了来自不同开发线中多个相关补丁的变更，并区分出合并补丁与被合并的补丁，从而让下游维护者能够轻松识别出整合后的修复方案。 对于镜像关系，LLM 会检查不同软件版本或分支中的补丁是否实现了相同或高度相似的修复方案，且代码变更和提交信息都具有高度的相似性。

sents.zh: 对于镜像关系，LLM 会检查不同软件版本或分支中的补丁是否实现了相同或高度相似的修复方案，且代码变更和提交信息都具有高度的相似性。

paragraphs.en: COMPASS then prompts the LLM to reason about dependency within the involved patch set, (e.g., whether a later patch is based on the earlier patch’s code, uses newly added or modified functions or variables, or whether the application order affects fixing effectiveness), which is explicitly described in the prompt . Based on the identified dependency characteristics and the semantic intent inferred from code changes and commit messages, the LLM further analyzes each relationship instance into Better Solution , Fixing-of-Fixing , or Collaboration . These three relationships reflect different dependency semantics, including refinement without security impact, correction of flaws introduced by earlier fixes, or complementary contributions toward a complete fix.
paragraphs.zh: COMPASS 随后会提示 LLM 对涉及的补丁集内部的依赖关系进行推理（例如，较晚的补丁是否基于较早补丁的代码、是否使用了新添加或修改过的函数或变量，或者应用顺序是否会影响修复效果），这些内容在提示中均有明确说明。 基于已识别的依赖特征以及从代码变更和提交信息中推断出的语义意图，LLM 会进一步将每种关系实例分析为“更优方案”“修复中的修复”或“协作”。 这三种关系反映了不同的依赖语义，包括在不影响安全性的情况下进行改进、修正早期修复所引入的问题，或为实现完整修复而做出的互补性贡献。

sents.en: These three relationships reflect different dependency semantics, including refinement without security impact, correction of flaws introduced by earlier fixes, or complementary contributions toward a complete fix.

paragraphs.en: For relationship instances where the LLM does not identify dependency within the involved patch set, COMPASS guides the LLM to further examine the nature of their contributions. Specifically, the LLM reasons whether the patches address different aspects of the vulnerability independently, or perform fixes at multiple code locations where the vulnerable pattern is replicated. When such evidence is observed, the relationship instance is considered to exhibit Separation .
paragraphs.zh: 对于 LLM 未识别出相关补丁集合中存在依赖关系的关系实例，COMPASS 会引导 LLM 进一步考察这些补丁贡献的性质。 具体而言，LLM 需要判断这些补丁是否独立处理了漏洞的不同方面，或者是否在多个重复出现漏洞模式的代码位置进行了修复。 当观察到此类证据时，该关系实例即被视为表现出“分离性”。

paragraphs.en: To further enhance the reasoning, we augment the Phase-3 prompt with one-shot demonstrations: for each of the six relationship types, one real-world multi-patch CVE example (not included in our benchmark) is provided as an illustration of the expected inference and output format.
paragraphs.zh: 为了进一步提升推理能力，我们在第 3 阶段的提示中加入了单样本演示：对于六种关系类型中的每一种，我们都提供了一个真实世界的多补丁 CVE 示例（该示例未包含在我们的基准测试中），用以说明预期的推理过程和输出格式。

paragraphs.en: Phase-4 performs a validation check over the inferred relationship instances. This phase prompts the LLM to review the inferred results and ensure their completeness and consistency with respect to both the input patch group and the hierarchy-specific constraints.
paragraphs.zh: 第 4 阶段对推断出的关系实例执行验证检查。 此阶段会提示 LLM 审查推断结果，并确保其完整性以及与输入片段组和层级特定约束的一致性。

sents.en: Phase-4 performs a validation check over the inferred relationship instances.
sents.zh: 第 4 阶段对推断出的关系实例执行验证检查。

sents.en: This phase prompts the LLM to review the inferred results and ensure their completeness and consistency with respect to both the input patch group and the hierarchy-specific constraints.
sents.zh: 此阶段会提示 LLM 审查推断结果，并确保其完整性以及与输入片段组和层级特定约束的一致性。

paragraphs.en: First, the validation step ensures patch coverage: every patch in the input patch group should participate in at least one relationship instance, except for patches that have been identified as not contributing to the vulnerability fixing . Second, the validation enforces hierarchy-aware labeling constraints. Relationship instances in Hierarchy-1 ( Merge and Mirror ) should be single-labeled, while instances in Hierarchy-2 ( Better Solution , Fixing-of-Fixing , and Collaboration ) may carry multiple labels, as a single patch sometimes plays multiple roles within the same instance at the commit granularity. For Hierarchy-3 ( Separation ), each instance is single-labeled, as it represents non-dependent patches and does not involve overlapping roles.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，验证步骤确保补丁覆盖：输入补丁组中的每个补丁都应至少参与一个关系实例，但已被认定为未对漏洞修复作出贡献的补丁除外。 其次，验证会强制执行层级感知的标签约束。 Hierarchy-1（Merge 和 Mirror）中的关系实例应仅有一个标签，而 Hierarchy-2（Better Solution、Fixing-of-Fixing 和 Collaboration）中的实例可能带有多个标签，因为单个补丁有时在提交粒度上会在同一实例中扮演多种角色。 对于 Hierarchy-3（Separation），每个实例都只有一个标签，因为它代表的是非依赖的补丁，且不涉及重叠的角色。

paragraphs.en: To the best of our knowledge, there is no existing technique specifically designed for predicting relationships of multiple vulnerability patches. We therefore compare COMPASS with two categories of baselines: learning-based baselines built on pre-trained models widely used in related patch and commit understanding tasks, and an LLM-only baseline that directly prompts the best-performing LLM in RQ1 without COMPASS’s structured pipeline (details of the baselines are provided in Section IV-B ).
paragraphs.zh: 据我们所知，目前尚无专门用于预测多个漏洞补丁之间关系的技术。 因此，我们将 COMPASS 与两类基线方法进行比较：一类是基于学习、构建在相关补丁和提交理解任务中广泛使用的预训练模型之上的基线方法；另一类是仅使用 LLM 的基线方法，该方法直接在 RQ1 中表现最佳的 LLM 上发出提示，而无需使用 COMPASS 的结构化流程（基线方法的详细信息见第 IV-B 节）。

paragraphs.en: We implement learning-based baselines by fine-tuning pre-trained models and cast the task as supervised classification over patch pairs. For a vulnerability description D ​ e ​ s ​ c Desc , and a patch pair with commit information M ​ s ​ g 1 Msg_{1} , M ​ s ​ g 2 Msg_{2} (including commit IDs, messages, and branch/version information) and code changes C ​ G 1 CG_{1} , C ​ G 2 CG_{2} , we construct the model input as T T = [[CLS], D ​ e ​ s ​ c Desc , [SEP], M ​ s ​ g 1 Msg_{1} , C ​ G 1 CG_{1} , [SEP], M ​ s ​ g 2 Msg_{2} , C ​ G 2 CG_{2} , [SEP]], which is tokenized by the backbone tokenizer with padding or truncation to meet the model’s length limit. We also attach a lightweight classification head to map the backbone output to a 6-dimensional vector corresponding to the six relationship types studied in this work. As a patch pair may exhibit multiple relationship labels at the commit granularity, we treat the task as multi-label prediction using thresholding on each dimension (thresholds tuned on the validation set). This yields three baselines, C ​ R CR , C ​ - ​ T ​ 5 C\text{-}T5 , and B ​ E ​ R ​ T BERT (fine-tuned from CodeReviewer, CodeT5, and BERT, respectively) .
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过微调预训练模型来实现基于学习的基线方法，并将该任务定义为对代码片段对的监督分类问题。 对于一个漏洞描述 D ​ e ​ s ​ c Desc ，以及一个包含提交信息的代码片段对 M ​ s ​ g 1 Msg_{1} , M ​ s ​ g 2 Msg_{2}（包括提交 ID、消息和分支/版本信息）及代码变更 C ​ G 1 CG_{1} , C ​ G 2 CG_{2} ，我们将模型输入构建为 T T = [[CLS], D ​ e ​ s ​ c Desc , [SEP], M ​ s ​ g 1 Msg_{1} , C ​ G 1 CG_{1} , [SEP], M ​ s ​ g 2 Msg_{2} , C ​ G 2 CG_{2} , [SEP]]，并通过主干模型的分词器进行分词，同时通过填充或截断使其符合模型的长度限制。 我们还附加了一个轻量级的分类头，用于将主干模型的输出映射到一个 6 维向量，该向量对应于本研究探讨的六种关系类型。 由于一个代码片段对在提交粒度上可能表现出多个关系标签，因此我们将该任务视为多标签预测问题，并对每个维度应用阈值判断（阈值在验证集上进行调整）。 由此得到了三种基线方法：C ​ R CR 、 C ​ - ​ T ​ 5 C\text{-}T5 和 B ​ E ​ R ​ T BERT（分别通过微调 CodeReviewer、CodeT5 和 BERT 得到）。

paragraphs.en: We construct a benchmark dataset of 300 multi-patch CVEs randomly selected from CVE [ 6 ] , NVD [ 7 ] , and Snyk [ 23 ] , spanning 2009 ∼ \sim 2024. This benchmark is completely disjoint from the 1,050 entries used for taxonomy construction in Section II . The benchmark CVEs cover 213 open-source repositories, including projects such as apache_tomcat , phpmyadmin , and linux . In terms of popularity, 70.0% of these repositories have more than 1K stars, including 20.7% with more than 10K stars and 31.0% with 3K ∼ \sim 10K stars. Meanwhile, 39.9% have more than 1K forks, including 7.0% with more than 10K forks and 8.9% with 3K ∼ \sim 10K forks. These statistics suggest that the benchmark involves many widely-used open-source projects.

paragraphs.en: The dataset contains 694 patches, where each CVE has 2 ∼ \sim 7 patches. For annotation, two experts having experience in software engineering and security independently labeled relationship instances, based on the vulnerability description and each patch’s information such as commit messages and code changes, strictly following guidelines aligned with the relationship descriptions in Section II . paragraphs.en: We evaluate COMPASS using Precision, Recall, and F1-score, classic effectiveness metrics for prediction tasks [ 66 , 67 , 68 , 69 ] , and report results for each relationship type (reporting metrics per relationship type mitigates the impact of potential minority classes) . The metrics are computed by matching predicted relationship instances against manually annotated instances. For each relationship type T ​ y ​ p ​ e Type , we collect: ( i ) the set of predicted relationship instances of this type across all CVEs, denoted by ℝ T ​ y ​ p ​ e \mathbb{R}_{Type} , ( ii ) the set of manually-annotated relationship instances for this type, denoted by 𝔾 T ​ y ​ p ​ e \mathbb{G}_{Type} . We then derive the set of correct predictions ℂ T ​ y ​ p ​ e \mathbb{C}_{Type} ⊆ \subseteq ℝ T ​ y ​ p ​ e \mathbb{R}_{Type} , where an instance is counted as correct only if it matches an annotated instance under the same type. Specifically, we match predicted and annotated relationship instances in a type-aware manner. For Merge , Better Solution , Fixing-of-Fixing , and Collaboration , an instance matches only if the dictionary’s key-value pairs are identical. For Mirror , if there is no designated subject patch (i.e., any patch can serve as the dictionary key), we ignore the key choice and match instances by their patch sets. For Separation , each patch alone forms an instance, so a match reduces to equality of p I ​ D ​ - ​ i p_{ID\text{-}i} . Given the above symbols, we calculate R ​ e ​ c ​ a ​ l ​ l T ​ y ​ p ​ e Recall_{Type} as | ℂ T ​ y ​ p ​ e | / | 𝔾 T ​ y ​ p ​ e | |\mathbb{C}_{Type}|/|\mathbb{G}_{Type}| , P ​ r ​ e ​ c ​ i ​ s ​ i ​ o ​ n T ​ y ​ p ​ e Precision_{Type} as | ℂ T ​ y ​ p ​ e | / | ℝ T ​ y ​ p ​ e | |\mathbb{C}_{Type}|/|\mathbb{R}_{Type}| , and F ​ 1 ​ - ​ S ​ c ​ o ​ r ​ e T ​ y ​ p ​ e F1\text{-}Score_{Type} as the harmonic mean of R ​ e ​ c ​ a ​ l ​ l T ​ y ​ p ​ e Recall_{Type} and P ​ r ​ e ​ c ​ i ​ s ​ i ​ o ​ n T ​ y ​ p ​ e Precision_{Type} .

paragraphs.en: COMPASS’s advantage is particularly evident on the dependency-driven relationships in Hierarchy-2. For Better Solution , Fixing-of-Fixing , and Collaboration , COMPASS attains F1-Scores of 62.50%, 69.23%, and 63.64%, respectively, greatly outperforming learning-based and LLM-only baselines. This gap suggests that instance-level dependency reasoning, which is explicitly guided by COMPASS’s hierarchical inference design, is difficult to recover through pairwise classification or LLM reasoning alone. For relationships whose evidence is more distinctive in code changes or version/branch context (rather than explicit message cues), the baselines exhibit improved effectiveness but still remain notably behind COMPASS. For example, on Merge and Mirror , the best baselines achieve F1-Scores of 59.17% and 76.12%, respectively, compared to 80.49% and 87.36% for COMPASS, respectively. paragraphs.zh: COMPASS 的优势在 Hierarchy-2 中依赖驱动的关系上尤为明显。 在“更优解决方案”、“修复的修复”和“协作”方面，COMPASS 分别取得了 62.50%、69.23% 和 63.64% 的 F1 分数，显著优于基于学习的方法和仅使用 LLM 的基线模型。 这一差距表明，实例级别的依赖推理——由 COMPASS 的分层推理设计明确引导——难以仅通过成对分类或 LLM 推理来恢复。 对于那些证据更多体现在代码变更或版本/分支上下文（而非显式消息提示）中的关系，基线模型的表现有所提升，但仍明显落后于 COMPASS。 例如，在“合并”和“镜像”任务中，最佳基线模型分别取得了 59.17% 和 76.12% 的 F1 分数，而 COMPASS 则分别达到了 80.49% 和 87.36%。 而在“分离”任务中，最佳基线模型达到了 61.22%，而 COMPASS 则取得了 82.86%。

paragraphs.en: Among the learning-based baselines, we further analyze the behavior of the soft-prompt variants, whose gains are limited and occasional. Notable improvements can be observed in multiple cases, for example, BERT-s increases Fixing-of-Fixing Recall from 28.00% ( BERT ) to 52.00%, and also improves Mirror Recall from 60.31% ( BERT ) to 79.23%. In contrast, some cases show little change, e.g., the F1-Score of Merge for CR-s is from 43.84% ( CR ) to 43.90%, and others even degrade, e.g., the Precision of Fixing-of-Fixing for C-T5-s drops from 17.02% ( C-T5 ) to 13.11%. paragraphs.en: We report the ablation results on two key designs of COMPASS: removing the one-shot demonstrations in Phase-3 ( C z ​ e ​ r ​ o ​ - ​ s ​ h ​ o ​ t C_{zero\text{-}shot} ) and using only the prediction stage ( C p ​ r ​ e ​ d ​ - ​ o ​ n ​ l ​ y C_{pred\text{-}only} , i.e., without the supporting phases), as shown in Table III . Overall, both variants degrade effectiveness across relationship types, indicating that the one-shot strategy and the full pipeline design contribute positively to instance-level relationship inference. Specifically, removing one-shot demonstrations leads to consistent F1-Score drops, with the largest degradations on the dependency-driven relationships in Hierarchy-2, e.g., Better Solution (from 62.50% to 52.94%), Fixing-of-Fixing (from 69.23% to 59.64%), and especially Collaboration (from 63.64% to 32.14%). On the other hand, removing the supporting phases also causes effectiveness losses on several types, notably Collaboration (from 63.64% to 36.11%) and Separation (from 82.86% to 51.08%), suggesting that Phase-2 and Phase-4 provide useful preparatory patch understanding and post-hoc validation for the final predictions.
paragraphs.zh: 我们报告了 COMPASS 两项关键设计的消融实验结果：移除第 3 阶段中的单样本演示（C_{zero\text{-}shot}），以及仅使用预测阶段（C_{pred\text{-}only}，即不包含辅助阶段），如表 III 所示。 总体而言，这两种变体在所有关系类型上的有效性均有所下降，表明单样本策略和完整流程设计对实例级别的关系推理具有积极影响。 具体而言，移除单样本演示会导致 F1 分数持续下降，其中在 Hierarchy-2 中依赖关系驱动的关系类型下降最为显著，例如 Better Solution（从 62.50% 降至 52.94%）、Fixing-of-Fixing（从 69.23% 降至 59.64%），尤其是 Collaboration（从 63.64% 降至 32.14%）。 另一方面，移除辅助阶段也会导致多种关系类型的有效性下降，特别是 Collaboration（从 63.64% 降至 36.11%）和 Separation（从 82.86% 降至 51.08%），这表明第 2 阶段和第 4 阶段为最终预测提供了有益的预备性补丁理解和事后验证。

paragraphs.en: Our study is subject to several threats to validity. First, the taxonomy and manual labels may involve subjective judgment. To mitigate this, we constructed the taxonomy with practitioner feedback (following well-established taxonomy construction practices in empirical software engineering), used a benchmark disjoint from the taxonomy construction set, and annotated each patch group by experts independently, achieving a Cohen’s Kappa of 87.98%. Second, data leakage is a potential risk for LLM-based software engineering techniques. In our study, this risk is extremely slim because the task-critical ground truth is the patch relationship label, rather than publicly available CVE or patch information. Such relationship labels were newly created by us and are not available in public vulnerability platforms or existing datasets. Moreover, D ​ S ​ - ​ o ​ n ​ l ​ y DS\text{-}only performs worse than COMPASS, suggesting that the gain does not merely come from memorization. Third, effectiveness may vary across ecosystems or projects. Our benchmark randomly samples 300 CVEs from CVE, NVD, and Snyk, spans 2009 ∼ \sim 2024, and covers 213 repositories, but larger-scale and industrial validation is still needed.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究面临若干效度威胁。 首先，分类体系和手动标注可能涉及主观判断。 为缓解这一问题，我们结合从业者的反馈构建了分类体系（遵循经验软件工程中成熟的分类体系构建实践），使用了与分类体系构建集分离的基准数据集，并由专家独立对每个补丁组进行标注，最终实现了 87.98% 的 Cohen’s Kappa 值。 其次，数据泄露是基于大语言模型（LLM）的软件工程技术可能面临的风险。 在我们的研究中，这一风险极低，因为任务关键的真实依据是补丁关系标签，而非公开可用的 CVE 或补丁信息。 这类关系标签由我们全新创建，在公开的漏洞平台或现有数据集中均不存在。 此外，D S - o n l y DS\text{-}only 的表现劣于 COMPASS，这表明其增益并非单纯源于记忆。 第三，有效性可能因生态系统或项目而异。 我们的基准数据集从 CVE、NVD 和 Snyk 中随机抽取了 300 个 CVE，时间跨度为 2009 ∼ \sim 2024 年，覆盖了 213 个仓库，但仍需更大规模和工业级的验证。

paragraphs.en: Prior studies have shown that multi-patch vulnerabilities are prevalent, but most of them focus on locating relevant fixes or characterizing the phenomenon, rather than inferring how patches of the same CVE relate to each other. Li et al. [ 8 ] and Tan et al. [ 9 ] conduct empirical studies on multi-patch vulnerability remediation and summarize common characteristics and scenarios. Hommersom et al. study automated identification and ranking of fix commits, and note that a vulnerability may correspond to multiple fixing commits in practice [ 10 ] . Woo et al. further investigate patch effectiveness and show that a non-trivial portion of disclosed fixes are incomplete and may require supplementary patches, which increases the complexity of downstream remediation [ 11 ] . Most relevant to our study, Xu et al. examine the quality of CVE–patch mappings and track patches across branches or repositories, highlighting that a CVE does not always map to a single patch and that equivalent fixes may appear in different development lines [ 4 ] . In contrast, COMPASS goes beyond identifying or characterizing multiple patches: it infers instance-level relationships within a patch group and outputs structured relationship instances that can directly guide downstream patch adoption.
paragraphs.zh: 先前的研究已经表明，多补丁漏洞普遍存在，但大多数研究都集中在定位相关修复方法或描述这一现象上，而非推断同一 CVE 的补丁之间如何相互关联。Li 等人 [ 8 ] 和 Tan 等人 [ 9 ] 对多补丁漏洞的修复进行了实证研究，并总结了其共同特征和典型场景。 Hommersom 等人研究了修复提交代码的自动化识别与排序，并指出在实践中，一个漏洞可能对应多个修复提交代码 [ 10 ] 。 Woo 等人进一步探讨了补丁的有效性，并发现已披露的修复方法中有一部分并非完整，可能需要补充补丁，从而增加了下游修复工作的复杂性 [ 11 ] 。 与我们研究最相关的是 Xu 等人的工作：他们检验了 CVE–补丁映射的质量，并追踪了跨分支或仓库的补丁，指出一个 CVE 并不总是对应单个补丁，且等效的修复方法可能出现在不同的开发线中 [ 4 ] 。 相比之下，COMPASS 不仅限于识别或描述多个补丁：它能推断出补丁组内实例级的关系，并输出结构化的关系实例，从而可以直接指导下游的补丁采用。

paragraphs.en: This paper studies the practically important yet under-explored problem of understanding relationships of multiple patches for the same vulnerability, which directly affects downstream patch adoption. We propose COMPASS, an automated LLM-based approach that predicts instance-level patch relationships under six recurring and actionable relationship types derived from qualitative analysis and developers validation. COMPASS outperforms both compact learning-based baselines and an LLM-only baseline on a benchmark of 300 multi-patch CVEs, the average improvement reaches 85.04%. We also release the benchmark and an online querying website to support community reuse.
paragraphs.zh: 本文研究了具有实际重要性但尚未得到充分探索的问题，即理解同一漏洞中多个补丁之间的关系，这一问题直接影响下游的补丁采用。 我们提出了 COMPASS，这是一种基于大型语言模型（LLM）的自动化方法，能够根据定性分析和开发者验证得出的六种常见且可操作的关系类型，预测实例级别的补丁关系。 在一个包含 300 个多补丁 CVE 的基准测试中，COMPASS 的表现优于基于紧凑学习的基线模型以及仅使用大型语言模型的基线模型，平均提升幅度达到 85.04%。 我们还发布了该基准测试和一个在线查询网站，以支持社区复用。
